questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'India and Her Neighbours' refers to.
questions.a: India shares its land and sea frontiers with many neighbours, Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Sri Lanka and the Maldives, and its destiny is tied to theirs, as Nelson Mandela's words remind us.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'India and Her Neighbours'.
questions.a: Geography is destiny's map: what touches a neighbour's shore soon touches ours.

questions.q: Under which section is 'India and Her Neighbours' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'India and Pakistan' refers to.
questions.a: Pakistan was founded on a religious basis at Partition in 1947; shared history, language and culture tie the two countries even when politics divides them, and peace remains in both peoples' interest.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'India and Pakistan'.
questions.a: Partition divided territory, not civilisation: the two countries share rivers, music and memory.

questions.q: Under which section is 'India and Pakistan' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'India and China: Himalayan Giants' refers to.
questions.a: Across the Himalayas lies China, an ancient civilisation and a modern giant; trade, pilgrim routes and the long border link India with China in cooperation and, at times, in contest.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'India and China: Himalayan Giants'.
questions.a: Two ancient neighbours meeting in modern times need wisdom as much as strength.

questions.q: Under which section is 'India and China: Himalayan Giants' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Southern and Western Neighbours' refers to.
questions.a: Across the Palk Strait, Sri Lanka's Buddhist and Tamil ties run deep into Indian history; the Maldives dots the Indian Ocean; westward, Iran shares centuries of language, poetry and trade with India.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Southern and Western Neighbours'.
questions.a: Every neighbour is a chapter of shared history: the sea and the desert carried culture as surely as armies carried fear.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Southern and Western Neighbours' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Sri Lanka, Maldives, Iran (source: gees202.txt, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Iran)
